h.strategy: After listing and negating default assumptions, keep only the negations that a general mechanism supports. Candidate mechanisms: parent quality (strong parents leave little room to improve and have more to lose), redundancy (duplicate or similar options dilute each other's contribution), and bottlenecks (an option matters little when it is not on the path to the output, however strong it is). Prefer predictions in which a usually helpful edit becomes neutral or harmful in a common context, or a usually harmful edit becomes harmless. Avoid conditions that only a few parents satisfy. Spread hypotheses across different edited fields and condition fields. Give at least four 'lower' predictions where the intuitive guess would be 'higher'.

hyps.why: With edge 5 removed, node 2 cannot reach the output, so a conv on edge 0->2 is bottlenecked and adds almost nothing.
Edge 1->2 only feeds node 2, which is cut from the output when edge 5 is none, so the conv is wasted.
Without edge 4, node 1 reaches the output only through the longer 1->2->3 route, so upgrading edge 0 matters less.
A second skip into the output node is redundant with the existing direct skip and dilutes the gain.
The direct skip already provides the identity path, so another skip into node 3 adds little.
Upgrading a 1x1 to a 3x3 gains less than replacing a none or pool op, because the edge already carries a useful conv.
Replacing a strong skip on the direct edge with a conv gives up the easy-optimization path, so the change is neutral or harmful.
With a strong conv path via node 1 already present, a second conv path into the output is redundant.
Filling an empty direct edge with a skip restores the identity path and gains far more than replacing any other op.
Removing edge 1->2 costs nothing when node 2 is already cut from the output, so it is less harmful than in other parents.
